dense-gqa: causal attention + GEMM/GEMV. Baseline: no engine in this repo records it as unsupported.
dense-mha: as above; the shape every paged-attention kernel was written for.
mla: **MLA decode kernel.** The cache is a shared low-rank latent + a decoupled RoPE key, not per-head K/V, so a GQA kernel cannot serve it. [[mla-latent-attention]]
sliding-window: local/windowed attention on some or all layers

**local-attention decode kernel + per-layer-type cache management.** The two layer classes have opposite scaling — a local layer's decode cost is constant in context, a global layer's grows — so one kernel serves both regimes. [[sliding-window-hybrid-attention]]
hybrid-attention-ssm: SSM / linear-attention layers interleaved with attention
**two kernel families plus a fixed-state allocator**: a chunked SSD or delta-rule kernel *and* an attention or MLA kernel. [[ssm-recurrent-state-update]] [[ssm-sequential-scan-tensor-core-mismatch]]
recurrent: RNN-style WKV update; **no chunk-parallel reformulation exists**, so it is the worst case for the tensor-core mismatch.
diffusion: **no KV cache and no decode loop.** Needs multi-token parallel decode and a block-diffusion sampler. [[diffusion-lm-denoising-steps]]
encoder-decoder: **three distinct things in one graph**: a bidirectional encoder with no cache, a decoder self-attention KV that grows, and a decoder cross-attention KV that is *constant per request*.
bi-encoder: one full-sequence forward + pooling. No cache, no incremental state. [[embedding-batch-encoding]]
cross-encoder: N independent full forwards, no cache reuse, no early exit. [[cross-encoder-reranking]]
speech-encoder: conv-augmented attention forward pass. **No engine record in this repo enumerates this class.**
multimodal: encoder tower on a *separate schedule* from the decoder, plus mrope / DeepStack in the decoder where present.
undisclosed: none derivable. The kernel question is **moot**, not unknown: no local engine serves these.

vllm.name: vLLM
best_for: Multi-user servers with high request concurrency, where continuous batching plus paged KV is what actually buys throughput
Workloads with heavy shared prefixes (long documents queried repeatedly, multi-turn chat) because automatic prefix caching removes repeated prefill
Broad model and quantization coverage when you want one engine rather than a per-quantization specialist
Production serving where an OpenAI-compatible API and Kubernetes-friendly serving options matter
avoid_for: Single-user laptop chat, where install size and startup cost dominate and nothing needs paged KV
Hardware without a maintained kernel path - every accelerator gain is tied to a bespoke kernel set that has to be compiled and validated per platform
Windows hosts, without accepting WSL
AMD GPUs when you need enc-dec models, multi-step scheduling, async output, or Marlin-kernel quantizations

sglang.name: SGLang
best_for: Agentic and RL workloads where many requests share long, branching context - the radix cache reuses partial prefixes, not just exact ones
Serving latency-sensitive multi-turn conversation, because prefix reuse removes the re-prefill of chat history
Teams that want to experiment with scheduling policy rather than just tune it
avoid_for: Environments pinned to CUDA 12 - there is no supported lane any more
Installs where a silently downgraded dependency is acceptable risk; the pre-release dependency set is a real operational hazard
Consumer AMD Radeon cards, which are not in the documented support list

tensorrt-llm.name: TensorRT-LLM
best_for: Maximum throughput on a fixed NVIDIA fleet, especially MoE models where expert parallelism and load balancing are the bottleneck
Deployments that can afford a build-time/version-lock step in exchange for hand-tuned kernels, CUDA graphs and the overlap scheduler
Latency-bound single-request serving on datacenter NVIDIA parts
avoid_for: Any non-NVIDIA accelerator
Environments where you cannot control the CUDA and PyTorch versions, or where an unexpected pip resolution would be unrecoverable
Teams that need to support many model architectures without NVIDIA adding support for each

flashinfer.name: FlashInfer
best_for: Squeezing attention and sampling throughput inside SGLang or vLLM on NVIDIA GPUs
Researching custom attention plans and sampling strategies against a real serving harness
As the default attention path when you have already committed to SGLang
avoid_for: Non-NVIDIA hardware, or NVIDIA parts below sm75
Environments where JIT compilation at runtime is unacceptable
Serving on its own - pair it with an engine

exllamav3.name: ExLlamaV3
best_for: Current-generation NVIDIA consumer cards: best-quality low-bit quants plus explicit MoE expert/tensor parallelism for machines that are not a datacenter.
Fitting a large MoE model into a single card with CPU offload for the leftover experts.
Single-user interactive decode speed where cache precision matters (2-8 bit cache).
Architecture coverage: the HF list is the broadest of any engine here.
Fast one-pass quantization from HF safetensors to EXL3.
avoid_for: AMD, Intel, or Apple hardware.
CPU-only inference — the CPU path exists but only as an offload target for MoE, not as the primary engine.
Simplicity: build-time CUDA/Triton setup is real work compared to llama.cpp or ONNX paths.
Serving workloads that need paged KV across many concurrent users; the generator does dynamic batching but the project is single-user oriented.

mlx-lm.name: MLX-LM
best_for: Local Mac development and personal use, where Metal is fast and battery/thermals matter
Quantized models from mlx-community that were converted specifically for MLX, since those are the tuned path
Fine-tuning or LoRA work on Apple Silicon, which mlx-lm supports natively including on quantized models
avoid_for: Any shared or multi-tenant server - you want vLLM-Metal (see [[vllm-metal]]) if you need paged KV and real continuous batching on a Mac
Non-Apple hardware, without exception
Workloads needing KV-cache quantization and request concurrency at the same time

vllm-metal.name: vLLM-Metal
best_for: Running vLLM's serving semantics (paged KV, continuous batching, prefix caching) on a Mac
Local development against a vLLM-compatible API on Apple Silicon
Serving a model that fits in unified memory with acceptable single-user latency
avoid_for: Multi-tenant datacenter serving - unified memory bandwidth does not compete with HBM
Non-Apple Silicon, or macOS older than 15
Production use where the plugin's release cadence and community-maintained status are unacceptable risk; upstream vLLM itself treats this as a community path
